Key sets

Source: R/keyset.R
jose_keyset.Rd

A jose_keyset holds several keys, as a JWK Set does (RFC 7517 section 5). Select one by kid with [[, or several with [; combine with c() or jose_keyset().

Usage

jose_keyset(...)

as_jose_keyset(x)

Arguments

...

jose_key and jose_keyset objects, combined in order.

x

JWK Set text, a parsed JWK Set, or a jose_keyset.

Value

A jose_keyset.

Details

as_jose_keyset() reads a JWK Set from its JSON text or from a parsed list. Following RFC 7517 section 5, a member of keys that is not a well-formed JWK is ignored rather than failing the whole set, as is a key of a type zujose does not know. A key of a known type that zujose cannot use, such as an Ed25519 OKP key, is kept: it can be listed, selected and thumbprinted, and using it raises zujose_unsupported_error.

Examples

set <- jose_keyset(
  jose_key_oct(as.raw(1:32), kid = "a"),
  jose_key_oct(as.raw(33:64), kid = "b")
)
set[["b"]]
#> <jose_key> oct, 256 bits
#>   kid "b"
#>   private: yes (not shown)
length(set)
#> [1] 2
